title: Update on my AI quorum strategy.
author: xspire
selftext:
Original post: [https://www.reddit.com/r/ai\_trading/s/ZRKayMq86r](https://www.reddit.com/r/ai_trading/s/ZRKayMq86r)

  
I got some responses and wanted to provide an update and a longer chart. So far with limited capital the quorum strategy with several AI agents arguing and establishing consensus on a position is working. The month chart is interesting because they were doing just meh with long positions then in late August I allowed options which caused the sharp dip. I worked on the options logic and then I've seen some robust gains. 

In the weekly chart you can see that the quorum has abandoned all non-option strategies and that's why the lines are flat during non-trading hours. 

The graphs look much better than my individual account. I think I'll slowly start shifting more capital towards this account but I worry how more available capital will influence them. 

Let me know your thoughts.

comments.author: jayyfo
comments.body:
What sort of options trades is it doing? What underlyings? I'm guessing only the ones with the most liquid options? What criteria for the trades? Spreads or single legged options? Buying premium or selling premium? What expiration dates? Do you have it also calculate and use the expected move? Indexes spx xsp?

How much do you pay for all the models you are using? Which ones? I'm super green ti this but not green ti trading and not green to technology, but I have been overwhelmed with the task of learning how to do this, could you maybe make or post a YouTube tutorial of how you put all this together?

replies.author: xspire
replies.body:
It's doing long put/call and vertical spreads. It doesn't have any shares to do covered calls and no cash for cash secured puts. It was doing september 18 dates this last week but today started moving out to october dates. It holds positions for a day or two. I basically have python and a shit ton of data calculate everything and feed it to the agents. so the agents only take in processed data and make their score cards. 

I spend around 100$/month on AI subscriptions. The token usage for the quorum is low compared to the engineering of the system. I've been using Fable and Sol consistently and the third agent i've swapped around.

replies.author: EmergencyFly6361
replies.body: What are the strategies or entry/exit conditions for long calls/puts and under which timeframe candles?

How did you? Any videos you can recommend? Or am I overthinking this? Is it easier to put them together? I've only ever used chatgpt free basically I don't even know what fable or sol is yet and how tokens work
